interleaving.how: question by question: all three arms answer question i before any arm sees question i+1, and the first arm rotates with i

grading.how: one extractor and one comparison for all three arms; number compares exact rationals through tasks/exact.mjs, exact compares characters. The winner is decided on this ruler and no other
grading.loose: accuracyLoose repeats the strict ruler with case ignored
grading.anywhere: accuracyAnywhere is the generous edge: the right answer is somewhere in what the arm wrote, wherever it is. It is reported, never used to pick a winner
grading.provenance: arms.<arm>.provenance counts each answer as exact (act/solve.mjs computed the whole prompt, with no model and no socket), memory (the retrieval answered) or model (the llm answered), with how many of each were right. The alone arm is the raw model and carries none

statement: organism won: 70/70 = 100.00% against null 67/70 = 95.71%, a gap of 4.29 points. The 95% interval is 5.20 points wide on the winner and 10.39 on the runner up, and a gap this size at these rates needs 86 questions per arm to separate from zero.

alone.candidate: Each input string is transformed by repeating the first digit three times and appending the rest of the string
Take the first digit, then the third digit, then the second digit, then the fourth digit
First part: input with leading zeros (4-digit), Second part: input × 249.95
First digit repeated four times, second digit repeated two times
